thread:
Jorge: quick sync 1 local fast-fallback logic vs cluster-wide capacity gating. leaning toward a token-bucket per-fallback-cluster + conservative local triggers. thoughts?

Mei: token-bucket makes sense. prevents many routers from flooding fallback infra simultaneously. need a clear refill policy and a backpressure signal.

Sam: +1. would add SLO-awareness: tokens consumed at different rates depending on expected cost (e.g., embedding model tokens=2, gen model tokens=1). that helps reserve capacity for heavy work.

Claire: also consider a spillover plan: when bucket empty, routers should route to secondary fallback variant (degraded but cheaper) rather than primary. avoids 503s.

Jorge: nice. propose components: 1) local watcher for short-window detection (median+p90) and soft ramp 2) cluster gate (token-bucket service) that issues tokens with TTL and credits 3) orchestration endpoint for manual overrides.

Mei: what about hysteresis? watchers need cooldown to avoid flip-flop. propose: once a router moves to strong-fallback, it must stay for min_stable_s (default 45s) unless operator forces revert.

Sam: add health-weighted scoring to token requests. request payload: {cluster,id,desired_fraction,weight_score}. response: {granted_fraction, token, ttl, reason}. use small protobuf for speed.

Claire: metrics contract: routers push aggregated records every 5s to rollout-metrics: {region,cluster,p50,p90,p99,err_rate,requests}. token-bucket service also emits credits_left per-cluster. orch aggregates for dashboards.

Jorge: edge case: network partition to token service. locals must operate in autonomous mode: allow emergency fallback only if scoring_exceeds_emergency_threshold (like p95>1s and err>0.2). also log event for audit.

Mei: OK. Also want a fast-rollback leash: if too many nodes fallback at once (>= 30% of cluster), run global rollback to prevent thrash. token-bucket can detect that and mark cluster as "throttled".

Sam: algorithm sketch for watcher:
```text
STATE: OBSERVE -> SOFT_RAMP -> TOKEN_REQUEST -> GUARDED_RAMP -> STABLE
OBSERVE: collect window 10s median+p90
SOFT_RAMP: route 5% for 5s to validate cache/warmth
TOKEN_REQUEST: ask token-bucket for extra fraction
GUARDED_RAMP: if token_granted ramp 25%->50%->100% else backoff
STABLE: cooldown 45s before new triggers
```

Claire: ops playbook: autopager when token-denied+high error. provide quick CLI: orch.force-fallback(cluster), orch.drain-pilot(cluster), orch.unwind(cluster). RBACed.

Jorge: operational safety: keep fallback capacity >= 20% for emergency use. token-bucket should reserve that pool and only release on explicit operator or very high severity.

Mei: implementation detail: make watcher a tiny Rust binary sidecar with a single outgoing dependency (HTTP/GRPC). no local DB. short-lived in-memory state only.

Sam: tests: create noisy-probe sim vectors, partition simulation (token service down), and overload-case where fallback infra slowly degrades. run chaos on each.

Claire: small addition: when returning traffic to primary, use asymmetric ramp: prioritize slow return to avoid cache cold-starts (e.g., 10%->30%->60%->100% with 15s steps).

cicd-bot: deployed a canary job for auto-fallback tests in staging (model=v4, region=ap-south).

Jorge: perfect. I'll draft a short RFC: API proto messages, watcher state diagram, token-bucket semantics, metrics topic schema, and ops runbook. @Mei can you stub the Rust sidecar repo? @Sam write the test vectors.

Mei: on it. will push skeleton tomorrow.

Sam: will add chaos scenarios.

Claire: will draft ops playbook and CLI commands.
